title: Truthfulness and trustworthiness
intro: A Muslim loves the truth and keeps what is entrusted to them – just like the Prophet (SAW), “al-Amin”, the trustworthy one.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) tells the believers to be mindful of Him and to speak only what is true and right. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Ahzab 33:70)</small>
Truthfulness is a good human quality: standing up for the truth and loving it. Muslim men and women are truthful, they lean towards the truth, and they keep away from lies.
A Muslim does not see truthfulness only as a nice extra quality – it is part of their faith.
Sometimes a Muslim has to confirm something with an honest word even when the truth goes against themselves or against someone they love. That is a real test of how truthful they are.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Say the truth, even if it is bitter.” (Ahmad)

Trustworthiness means keeping your promises and taking good care of what was entrusted to you. The Qur’an describes the believers as those who keep the trusts given to them and keep their promises. (Qur’an, Al-Ma‘arij 70:32)

A trustworthy person does not betray what someone trusted them with, and keeps what they agreed with others. The Prophet (SAW) called people who break their promises hypocrites (people who are two-faced).
Life in this world is full of trusts (amanah) and duties that we must carry out, and we are responsible for how we treat them.

Even before he became a prophet, the Prophet (SAW) was known among his people as al-Amin – the trustworthy one. Khadijah (RA), a rich and respected woman, married him because of his trustworthiness and good character. Even before their marriage she trusted him to take her goods for trade to faraway Sham (Syria).

Because of his trustworthiness, even the Quraysh – who did not believe he was a prophet – left their valuables with him. When Allah (SWT) ordered him to make the Hijrah to Madinah, after his people had treated him badly, he left Ali (RA), his cousin, behind to return everything people had left with him. He was the most trustworthy man.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “There is no faith in the one who cannot be trusted, and no religion in the one who does not keep his promises.” (Ahmad)
Losing trustworthiness means losing faith – and it is one of the signs of the Day of Judgement. The Prophet (SAW) said: “When trust is lost, then wait for the Hour.” (Bukhari)
Trustworthiness and trust are the qualities on which good relations in society are built.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: The marks of a good Muslim are trustworthiness, sincerity and truthfulness. Try hard so that others recognise you by them!

practice.title: A truthful and trustworthy Muslim
practice.prompt: Tap everything a truthful and trustworthy Muslim does, then tap Check.

options.text: 🗣️ Says the truth even when it is hard
🔒 Takes care of what friends lend them
↩️ Gives back what belongs to others
🤥 Tells a small lie to get out of trouble
options.why: The Prophet (SAW) said: say the truth, even if it is bitter.

options.text: 📢 Shares a secret a friend trusted them with
options.why: A secret is also an amanah (a trust) – a trustworthy person keeps it.

options.text: ⏳ Agrees to meet but never comes
options.why: Breaking promises is a sign of a hypocrite, not of a believer.

practice.title: The story of al-Amin
practice.prompt: Put the events in the right order.
items: Muhammad (SAW) is known among his people as al-Amin, the trustworthy one
Khadijah (RA) trusts him with her goods for trade in Sham
Khadijah (RA) marries him because of his trustworthiness and good character
Allah orders him to make the Hijrah to Madinah
Ali (RA) stays behind to give people back their valuables

options: Loving and standing up for the truth

questions.q: What nickname did the Prophet (SAW) have even before he was a prophet?
What did the Prophet (SAW) say about the one who does not keep promises?
Who returned the Quraysh’s valuables after the Hijrah?
